Subject: Post-demo: Rerank & Embeddings evaluation vs hyperscalers — next tests

Hi Avery / Ben —

Thanks again for the hour today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of next tests so we can compare Redwood's reranking/embeddings pipeline with what you were hedging toward on the hyperscalers. High level takeaways:

- You care most about: retrieval recall@10 (domain docs), end-to-end retrieval + rerank latency (p95), and per-query cost at scale (x100k/day).
- You currently evaluate an embeddings + ANN index (FAISS/HNSW) on Vertex and an API-based rerank path against Bedrock + a hosted re-ranker.

Proposed next tests (short & prioritized):
1) Recall sweep: run recall@1/5/10 over your 20k seed queries vs our default 1536-dim embeddings + HNSW and match against your Vertex baseline (same dataset/queries).
2) Latency P95: measure cold-start and warm cache p95 for retrieval-only and retrieval+rerank (end-to-end) at 1qps and 50qps, record CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Cost modelling: estimate per-query cost for both approaches (tokenized reranker on GPU vs remote API reranker on hyperscaler) including network egress and embedding storage costs.
4) Dim & quant sweep: compare 1536-dim vs 1024-dim (quantized int8) embeddings to see tradeoffs in recall and vector storage.

I've attached a lightweight eval plan template (novasearch-eval-plan-20260318.xlsx) — fills in dataset paths and suggested scripts. If you approve, we (Redwood) can run the first two tests using a shared subset of your corpus or you can run them and share the CSV outputs.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) which dataset subset you'd like us to use (e.g., 20k doc subset you mentioned), (b) whether we should spin up a temporary dedicated instance to run rerank on GPU, and (c) whether you prefer Redwood to run tests or hand off scripts?

Cheers,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Rafael —

Thanks for the detailed recap. That plan looks very reasonable. A few clarifications from our side:

- Dataset: let's start with the 25k doc subset (news + product manual mix) — I'll share a transient S3 link.
- Ownership: we'd prefer Redwood to run the initial benchmarks if you can include the raw latency traces and the CSVs for recall.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence for any temporary instance. Can you point me at a short attestation?

Ben — you and I can pair on the exact queries set. My target is to see whether recall@10 improves materially when we move rerank onto a colocated GPU versus calling a hyperscaler re-ranker API (network + op cost tradeoff).

Also, can we get a cost delta: - Hyperscaler embeddings + hosted reranker (per 1M queries) vs - Redwood-hosted reranker on a small dedicated pool (monthly amortized)? Even a ballpark figure will help with procurement.

Appreciate it — Avery

Hi Avery / Ben —

Thanks — great to meet you both. Quick technical notes and what we'll deliver if Redwood runs the tests: 

Deliverables (first run):
- recall_results.csv: recall@1/5/10 for 25k docs + 2k seed queries (same query set you use) comparing:
  a) Vertex embeddings (1536d) + your HNSW index
  b) Redwood embeddings (1536d, FP16) + HNSW (our infra)
  c) Redwood embeddings (1024d, int8 quant) + HNSW
- latency_traces/ : p50/p95/p99 for retrieval-only and retrieval+rerank (cold & warm).
- cost_estimate.md: per-1M query cost breakdown (embedding storage, ANN cost, rerank token cost, network).

Bench specifics / config we'll use:
- Embedding dims: 1536 (baseline) and 1024 (reduced/quantized).
- ANN: HNSW parameters (M=16, efConstruction=200, efSearch=128) to mirror your current build; we'll also run an IVF+PQ pass for comparison if you want.
- Reranker: sequence-pair re-ranker on a small GPU instance (A100/80GB equiv) with batching tuned to maintain p95 < 200ms for the rerank step in the warm case.
- Warm vs cold: warm means warmed ANN and warmed model container (simulate steady traffic); cold means fresh container + cold disk-backed index.

Security note: Rafael — we will attach SOC2 summary and our SOC2 contact card. Avery, Redwood will only access the S3 subset you share temporarily; we can delete after benchmarks and provide logs.

Estimated timelines: 3 business days to run the base recall + latency tests once we have the S3 link and credentials. I'll hand off the result CSVs and a short readme.

Questions for NovaSearch:
- Which ANN hyperparams (if any) are you already using beyond the defaults? You mentioned efSearch is 128 but we need efConstruction and M.
- Any PII redaction rules for the 25k subset? If present, we'll follow.

If you prefer to run locally, I can provide the scripts (python + jupyter) and a small Docker image — but running it from Redwood will let us show the end-to-end production metrics easily.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
